extracted.intended_audience: implementers and authors of MathML processors, renderers, browsers, editors, and other MathML-aware applications
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance for embedding, serializing, transferring, and mixing MathML with host environments (HTML/XHTML/other formats), and for use of semantics/id/xref, annotations, and transfer flavors. Targets developers of browsers, equation editors, CMSs, and other MathML-producing or -consuming software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of id and xref within semantics to establish cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: An id attribute and associated xref attributes that appear within the same semantics element establish cross-references between corresponding sub-expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For parallel markup, all id attributes referenced by any xref should be in the same branch of an enclosing semantics element to avoid unintentional cycles. id and xref may be placed on MathML elements of any type. It is often useful to put id attributes on the branch with the finest-grained node structure; in absence of other criteria the first branch of semantics is a sensible choice. Cross-references may be used in any semantic annotations within annotation-xml (e.g., cross-referencing a presentation rendering and an OpenMath annotation). Direction of references does not imply selection is permitted only on one child; selecting a subtree in any branch and recovering corresponding subtrees is equally feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize MathML in XML by namespace URI
rubrics_metrics.description: Within an XML document supporting namespaces, the preferred method to recognize MathML markup is by the identification of the math element in the MathML namespace by the MathML namespace URI http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MathML namespace URI is the recommended method to embed MathML within XHTML documents. Markup-language specifications embedding MathML should use similar conditions and keep local names of MathML elements as defined by this recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize MathML in HTML using HTML parser behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: HTML has built-in knowledge of the MathML namespace: the math element and its descendants will be placed in the MathML namespace by the HTML parser and will appear as if the input had been XHTML with the namespace declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See parser-specific rules (later sections) for detailed handling and mixing rules when using the HTML parser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names and media types for MathML encodings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the defined encoding names to distinguish MathML-Presentation, MathML-Content, and MathML (generic); each has specified media types, clipboard flavors, and UTIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML-Presentation: Media Type application/mathml-presentation+xml, Windows Clipboard Flavor 'MathML Presentation', UTI public.mathml.presentation. MathML-Content: application/mathml-content+xml, 'MathML Content', UTI public.mathml.content. MathML (generic): may contain presentation, content, or mixture; file extension .mml; media type application/mathml+xml; UTI public.mathml. The MathML 2 predefined encoding values MathML, MathML-Content, MathML-Presentation may be used for backward compatibility on annotation-xml encoding attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: When transferring MathML: well-formed XML and root/math namespace requirements (MUSTs)
rubrics_metrics.description: When transferring MathML, an application MUST ensure the content of the data transfer is a well-formed XML instance of a MathML document type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: the instance MAY begin with an XML declaration; the instance MUST contain exactly one root math element; the instance MUST declare the MathML namespace on the root math element; the instance MAY use a schemaLocation attribute; the instance SHOULD use numeric character references rather than character entity names for greater interoperability; the instance MUST specify the character encoding if it uses an encoding other than UTF-8 (via XML declaration or BOM for UTF-16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use media types outside namespace-aware environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside of environments where XML namespaces are recognized, media types (RFC2045/RFC2046) should be used if possible to ensure invocation of a MathML processor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For environments where media types are not appropriate (e.g., clipboard formats), use the encoding names described for transfer flavors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and name transfer flavors exactly as specified
rubrics_metrics.description: The flavor names listed in Names of MathML Encodings are the exact strings that should be used to identify transfer flavors corresponding to MathML encodings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On operating systems that allow it, applications should register support for these flavor names (e.g., RegisterClipboardFormat on Windows, UTI on Mac).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer available MathML flavors when exporting (SHOULD/MUST guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that supports pure presentation markup and/or pure content markup SHOULD offer as many of the MathML flavors as it has available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application only exports one MathML flavor it SHOULD name it MathML. If able to determine a more specific flavor, it SHOULD offer both generic and specific transfer flavors, but only deliver the specific flavor if it knows the recipient supports it (e.g., via HTTP Accept header). Applications exporting both specific flavors SHOULD export content, presentation, and the generic flavor which SHOULD combine the other two using a top-level semantics element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer annotation-specific transfer flavors when semantics is sole child
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application exports a MathML fragment whose only child of the root element is a semantics element, it SHOULD offer, after the standard flavors, a transfer flavor for each annotation or annotation-xml element provided the transfer flavor can be recognized and named based on the encoding attribute value and the annotation key is alternate-representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer content for each annotation should contain character data in specified encoding (for annotation), a well-formed XML fragment (for annotation-xml), or the data obtained by requesting the URL in src (for annotation reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a plain-text fallback flavor (MAY) and ordering of flavors
rubrics_metrics.description: As a final fallback, an application MAY export a version of the data in a plain-text flavor (e.g., text/plain, CF_UNICODETEXT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple versions exist, the application may choose which to export as text at its discretion. The text version SHOULD generally omit the XML declaration, DOCTYPE, and other XML prolog material; the Unicode text version SHOULD always be the last flavor exported, following the principle that exported flavors are ordered from most specific to least specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process math, semantics, annotation, annotation-xml even if only one vocabulary implemented
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine whether a MathML instance is pure content or presentation markup, math, semantics, annotation, and annotation-xml elements should be regarded as belonging to both vocabularies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, an application that consumes MathML should always process these four elements, even if it only implements one of the two vocabularies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle external references cautiously; consumers may ignore unresolved references
rubrics_metrics.description: References to external resources (stylesheets, images, etc.) in MathML data can cause interoperability problems if the consumer cannot locate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers using external references should make users aware of potential problems and provide alternate ways to obtain referenced resources. Consumers that encounter references they cannot resolve or do not understand should ignore the external references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of attributes/elements from non-MathML namespaces
rubrics_metrics.description: In the standard schema, attributes from other namespaces are permitted on MathML elements but elements from other namespaces are not allowed (except in annotation-xml).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML processors encountering unknown XML markup should silently ignore attributes from non-MathML namespaces. An element from a non-MathML namespace should be treated as an error except in an annotation-xml element. If such an element is a child of a presentation element it should be handled as described in 3.3.5 Error Message <merror>; if a child of a content element it should be handled as described in 4.2.9 Error Markup <cerror> (e.g., render fraction with denominator indicating the error).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extending schema to allow foreign markup in token elements (design guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When designing a compound document format that includes MathML, the designer may extend MathML's content model to allow additional elements (e.g., allow non-MathML namespace elements in token elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML processors encountering unknown markup should follow the error-handling rules above. Example provided showing how to override mtext in Relax NG to allow any well-formed XML not in MathML namespace as a child of mtext, but this may be too lax; designers may only allow specific host-document inline elements instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storing private data within MathML without altering content model
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that needs to persist private data within a MathML expression should generally attempt to do so without altering the underlying content model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies: for small amounts of data, use attributes from other namespaces on MathML elements (when XML namespaces allowed); for larger amounts, use the semantics element (annotation/annotation-xml); to associate actions with presentation subtrees (e.g., mark incomplete expressions), use maction element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing MathML and XHTML: extensions to mtext and validity concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: To integrate MathML into XHTML it should be possible to embed XHTML in MathML; the HTML5 validator schema extends mtext to allow all inline (phrasing) HTML elements (including svg) as content of mtext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML fragments using XHTML elements within mtext will not be valid MathML if extracted and used in isolation; editing tools may offer support for removing HTML markup from mtext and replacing with text alternatives. Generally XHTML elements like headings, paragraphs, lists are often unnecessary in mathematical contexts since MathML provides math-specific constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing MathML and non-XML contexts (TeX-like syntax guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-XML vocabularies (e.g., TeX-like syntax) that parse to a tree that may be validated against the MathML schema may be viewed as MathML applications, but documents using such a system are not valid MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations of such syntaxes should, if possible, offer output of expressions in the XML MathML syntax so the application can be an MathML-output-conformant processor (see conformance section).

rubrics_metrics.name: HTML parser differences affecting MathML usage
rubrics_metrics.description: HTML parsing differs from XML parsing in important ways that affect MathML usage: attribute values may not need quoting, end tags may be omitted, HTML does not support namespace prefixes, and the HTML parser is defined to accept any input string producing a defined result (possibly a parse error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because HTML parser ignores namespace prefixes, using prefixed MathML like <mml:math ...> is problematic. Unless inside token elements or inside an annotation-xml with encoding text/html or application/xhtml+xml, presence of an HTML element will terminate the math expression by closing all open MathML elements; following MathML elements are then parsed as invalid HTML elements. Authors and tools should use MathML fragments that are well-formed XML even when embedded in HTML and offer a way to export MathML in a portable XML syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking rules: href and id usage
rubrics_metrics.description: In MathML, an element is designated as a link by the presence of the href attribute; MathML allows href on all elements. The id attribute should be used to specify link targets and must be unique within a document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most user agents cannot implement nested links or links on elements with no visible rendering; those links may have no effect. Certain presentation elements that do not ordinarily have visual rendering (mprescripts, malignmark, maligngroup) should not be used as linking elements. Generators aiming for MathML-Core compatibility may restrict href to the a element or provide a polyfill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use semantics/annotation-xml to provide graphical or alternative representations
rubrics_metrics.description: To embed additional graphical content or alternative representations (e.g., SVG, XHTML img, TIFF), use semantics with annotation-xml children encoding the alternative formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first child of semantics is typically the MathML-Content representation and is most analogous to img's alt attribute — suitable for non-visual rendering. A MathML processor can choose any of the representations for display (e.g., using SVG for graphical rendering). Example provided embedding SVG and XHTML img as annotation-xml alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using CSS with MathML (guiding observation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlling math style properties with CSS is desirable in environments that support CSS, but MathML layout schemata differ substantially from CSS visual formatting and many math layout parameters have no direct textual analogues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that support MathML natively may choose to (text cuts off here) — implementers should be aware of differences and that sensible CSS mappings may not be straightforward.
